solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Greeting the Spanish commended at first — in women, mostly

indicators.note: in says the Spanish article and the initial go inside the shortened women
mostly means nearly all of the word women is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: el is the Spanish for 'the'

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of commended

explanation.surface: A greeting addressed to a group of women, with praise for something done.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm reception given to an arriving guest is a form of greeting, so the noun fits.

clue.text: Flightless bird in Prague museum

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the letters of the words Prague museum, across the gap

explanation.surface: A stuffed flightless bird on display in a museum in the Czech capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Australian ratite cannot fly, a standard example of a flightless bird.

clue.text: Rodent initially caught on yellow plant, unfortunately

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the five words that follow it

explanation.surface: A rodent unluckily snagged on a yellow-flowered plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks as if it applies only to 'caught', but it takes the first letter of every word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The large South American water-dwelling animal, also called nutria, is a rodent.

clue.text: Tiny worker marking time on watch, perhaps?

parts.note: something tiny is minute, very small
a hand is a manual worker, as on a farm or ship

explanation.surface: A small labourer keeping time while on sentry duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' suggests a guard's shift, but it is the timepiece; 'perhaps' flags that a clock has one too.
explanation.definitionFit: The longer pointer on a clock face or wristwatch indicates the minutes, so it marks time.

clue.text: Persian ruler's quiet expression of satisfaction

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
ah is a sigh of contentment

explanation.surface: A Persian monarch letting out a soft sigh of contentment.
explanation.definitionFit: The title used by the kings of Iran, formerly Persia, until 1979.

clue.text: Composer upset about pistol case

parts.note: Gustav Holst, English composer of The Planets

indicators.note: upset, in a down clue, turns the short word for about upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A musician annoyed about something to do with a gun case.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather sheath worn on a belt or under the arm to carry a handgun.

clue.text: Shrub in untidy garden surrounded by fresh hay

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the jumbled garden inside the jumbled hay
fresh signals a new arrangement of the letters of hay
untidy says the letters of garden are put in disorder

explanation.surface: A bush growing in a messy garden ringed by newly cut hay.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'untidy' and 'fresh' read as plain description of the scene, yet each is an anagram signal; the shuffled hay (HYA) wraps the shuffled garden (DRANGE).
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering bush with big round heads of blue, pink or white blooms.

clue.text: Resilient young male worker inspiring union leader

indicators.note: inspiring, literally breathing in, has the first pair taking in the initial letter

parts.note: a boy is a young male

indicators.note: leader asks for the opening letter of union

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's usual worker insect

explanation.surface: A tough young labourer who motivates the head of a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stays cheerful and bounces back from setbacks is described with this word.

clue.text: Some strapping lad entering forest clearing

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A burly young man walking into an open space in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: An open grassy space among trees is a clearing in a forest.

clue.text: Brought from a distance? That's unbelievable!

definitions.meaning: literally fetched from far off, the word's original sense
an exclamation at a story too improbable to credit

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase once meant carried from afar and now describes an implausible tale or excuse.

clue.text: Military tribunal heard top officer when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking says the words are to be taken as they sound when said out loud

parts.note: heard is caught (did you catch that?), and a top officer is a marshal, as in field marshal

explanation.surface: A tribunal of soldiers listens while the senior commander gives evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the two words sound alike in pairs: 'caught' rhymes with the first part and 'marshal' with the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A court convened by the armed forces to try members accused of breaking military law.

clue.text: Woodworker's writing instrument pinched by carrier

indicators.note: pinched by says the pen is squeezed in, held within the carrier

parts.note: a carter carries goods by cart
a pen is something to write with

explanation.surface: A joiner's pen is stolen by a delivery man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinched' suggests stolen, but here it means gripped inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesperson who makes and repairs wooden structures and fittings works with wood.

clue.text: Slight breeze extremely rare in Somerset city

indicators.note: in puts those end letters inside the city

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, a county in south-west England

indicators.note: extremely asks for the end letters of the word rare

explanation.surface: A rare light wind blowing through a West Country city.
explanation.definitionFit: A breath of wind or air is a faint movement of it, a slight breeze.

clue.text: Sick inmate nursing ultimately fatal illness

indicators.note: nursing means holding, so the scrambled inmate cradles that last letter
sick says the letters of inmate are in a bad way, scrambled
ultimately asks for the final letter of fatal

explanation.surface: An ill prisoner tending someone with a deadly disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick' reads as describing the inmate, but it signals rearranging INMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor or chronic sickness or complaint is a synonym for illness.

clue.text: Scavenge at great length, never finishing

indicators.note: never finishing says the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: for ages means for a very long time

explanation.surface: An animal hunting for scraps endlessly without ever completing the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To search widely for food or provisions, as animals do, is to scavenge.

clue.text: Big tree a jazzman originally identified in Washington

indicators.note: in places the jazzman and the initial inside the abbreviation

parts.note: WA is the abbreviation for Washington State
Duke Ellington, American jazz bandleader and composer

indicators.note: originally asks for the first letter of identified

explanation.surface: A giant tree that a jazz musician first spotted in Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant sequoia was named this in Britain after the Duke of Wellington, and is a very large tree.

clue.text: Original, having first half of month on lake

indicators.note: first half of asks for the opening four of the month's eight letters

parts.note: November is a month
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Something new happening at a lake in the early part of a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A new idea, unlike anything before, can be called original.

clue.text: Control male ox

definitions.meaning: to guide or direct, as with a vehicle
a young castrated bull raised for beef

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to guide a vehicle's course; the noun names a castrated bullock.

clue.text: Trembling, seeing second colony of bees by railway

parts.note: a hive is the home of a bee colony, and by extension the colony

explanation.surface: Someone shaking after spotting another swarm of bees next to the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaking with cold or fear is described as trembling.

clue.text: Dreary routine involving stags in autumn

definitions.meaning: a monotonous groove that is hard to escape
the autumn mating season of deer, when stags fight

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a boring fixed habit and also the annual breeding season of deer.

clue.text: Time to abandon hackneyed ceremony

indicators.note: to abandon says the time letter leaves the word for hackneyed

parts.note: trite means overused, hackneyed

explanation.surface: It is time to drop a tired, stale ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious or solemn ritual act is a ceremony.

clue.text: Fawn upon grown-up relative finally touring area

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the first pieces surround the area letter

parts.note: an adult is a grown-up

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of relative

explanation.surface: An adult relative goes travelling around a region, sucking up to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fawn' could be a young deer or a colour; here it is the verb to flatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatter someone excessively and admire them slavishly is to fawn upon them.
